claims.text: Increasing the aluminum content of an HEA bond coat promotes alumina formation during HVOF processing.
Aluminum enrichment produces a continuous, dense Al2O3 layer during HVOF processing.
The alumina layer caused by aluminum enrichment increases bond-coat durability and reliability during high-temperature oxidation.
CrMnFeCoNi or related HEA bond coats without aluminum enrichment form non-uniform, less-protective oxide scales under HVOF conditions.
The proposed aluminum-enrichment treatment should remain effective during oxidation in air at approximately 1000 °C.
Aluminum diffuses from the HEA toward the particle or coating surface during HVOF processing.
Surface-directed aluminum diffusion leads to nucleation and growth of a continuous protective Al2O3 layer.
Aluminum reacts with oxygen during HVOF deposition to form surface Al2O3.
The resulting alumina scale is dense and acts as a barrier to further oxidation.
Aluminum enrichment prevents formation of less-protective mixed oxides.
Aluminum-enriched bond coats will develop a more uniform and adherent alumina scale than standard HEA bond coats.
Aluminum enrichment will reduce oxide penetration and oxide-scale growth rate.
Aluminum enrichment will improve coating adhesion and durability.
Standard HEA bond coats form heterogeneous, manganese-rich mixed oxide scales that cause inferior oxidation resistance and durability during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
There is an optimal aluminum-content range that enhances alumina formation without significantly changing the desired phase equilibria or mechanical properties.
Excessive aluminum addition may destabilize the alloy or impair its microstructural performance.
